runtime: Ubuntu (Linux 5.15), bash 5.x, python 3.12, azure-cli installed. Offline unit tests run with python3 -m unittest; dry-run and the display-name collision guard were exercised against a live tenant using an existing Azure CLI login.
procedure: 1. bash -n on the script. 2. python3 -m unittest tests.test_graph_readonly_app (9 cases: syntax, missing arguments, missing certificate file, unknown --app-id, ReadWrite refusal, FullControl refusal, Mail.Send refusal, ReadBasic acceptance, and that a Read permission whose name contains 'Management' is accepted). 3. Run with --dry-run against a signed-in tenant using an unused display name and confirm the tenant, identity and 12 default permissions are listed with no change. 4. Run WITHOUT --dry-run against the same tenant using a display name that already exists, and confirm the run stops before creating or crediting anything.
expected: Argument and permission validation reject bad input before any directory call. Only read forms pass. An application is never adopted by display name; a collision stops the run and reports the application ids found.
observed: All nine offline cases passed. --dry-run with an unused name listed the tenant, identity and 12 permissions and exited 0 without creating anything. The apply run against an existing display name exited 1, printed the colliding application id and the instruction to verify ownership and use --app-id, and made no change. Two weaknesses in the previous revision were the reason for this one: the write filter was a substring denylist that let Mail.Send through, and an existing application matching the display name was silently adopted and credentialed.
limitations: The create path and the --app-id update path have not been executed against a directory by this script. The equivalent az ad app create / credential reset / appRoleAssignments calls were performed manually and succeeded, but that does not certify this script.
Failure handling when the caller lacks directory write access is untested.
The collision guard compares display names only. It does not inspect application owners; the operator must verify ownership before passing --app-id.
No tenant identifiers are recorded here; the target tenant is not disclosed.
